mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rate signals accommodative monetary policy, reducing equity discount rates and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in 60%+ of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.25% (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 6.0% indicates tight labor market with accelerating wage growth, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60%+ of UNRATE < 6.0% periods (p-value > 0.05 vs baseline in t-test).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal robust consumer demand, accelerating economic growth and driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Joint signal (HOUST↑ and RSAFS↑) fails to predict positive 20-day returns in 60%+ cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows).

mechanism_narrative: Late-cycle expansion intensifies supply chain constraints, triggering inflationary pressures and central bank rate hikes, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in 60%+ of late-cycle periods (defined by INDPRO growth > 2% annualized and GDP > 2.5%).

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) reflects strong demand and economic growth, supporting corporate profit margins and driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in 60%+ of CPIAUCSL > 2.0% YoY periods (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 0.5% signals active monetary tightening, increasing borrowing costs and reducing equity valuations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60%+ of FEDFUNDS > 0.5% periods (p-value > 0.05 vs baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent payroll growth (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) indicate labor market strengthening, boosting consumer confidence and spending, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Joint signal (PAYEMS↑ and UNRATE↓) fails to predict positive 60-day returns in 60%+ cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows).

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles characterized by rising federal funds rates suppress economic activity and equity valuations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60%+ of monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25% in 3 months).
